strategy.observation: Linear positions itself as a system for product development and says it powers over 40,000 product teams.
strategy.offer_link: A company that serves product teams at that scale is likely to have ongoing customer research needs, so a service that recruits and schedules interview participants could save the product team time and keep feedback loops moving.
hypotheses: The Head of Product is involved in customer research or research operations.
Linear’s product team regularly runs customer interviews to inform roadmap decisions.
Recruiting and scheduling participants is a meaningful administrative burden for their team.
strategy.angle: Linear powers over 40,000 product teams, so I wondered if your product team ever wants a lighter way to keep customer interviews booked and flowing.
strategy.fit_reason: Linear is explicitly product-team-focused, and a product org at a company like this plausibly runs customer interviews often enough that participant recruiting and scheduling could be useful.

draft.subject: Interview logistics for product teams
draft.body:
Linear powers over 40,000 product teams. If your product team runs customer interviews regularly, recruiting and scheduling participants can turn into busywork.

I help product teams handle that part so researchers and PMs spend less time chasing calendars and more time in the interviews.

Who usually owns interview logistics on your side?
